breaking_news.headline: Family income rose and poverty fell in 2025 — but safety net cuts could erase gains
breaking_news.summary: An annual report from the Census Bureau shows the average family made more money in 2025 than the year before, while the official poverty rate declined. Health care coverage was little changed from 2024.

breaking_news.headline: CBO says Iran war driving up inflation, puts price tag at $38 billion
breaking_news.summary: Two new, independent reports show detailed looks at the costs of the war in Iran. It's led to shortages in U.S. weapons, supply chain bottlenecks and a price tag in the tens of billions of dollars.

breaking_news.headline: Turkish habit of stashing gold "under the pillow' hurts economy, government says
breaking_news.summary: For years, Turks have stashed their gold at home against a raining day, mistrustful of banks. Now the government says that tradition hurts the economy

breaking_news.headline: Why Steve Bannon sided with Sanders, not Trump, on AI
breaking_news.summary: Where does Steve Bannon fit in the debate over regulating or slowing AI? He tells Morning Edition where he breaks with Trump and what he thinks Washington should do.

breaking_news.headline: The Fed raises interest rates for the first time in over three years
breaking_news.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate Wednesday to combat stubborn inflation. That will make it more expensive to borrow money to buy a car or carry a balance on a credit card.

breaking_news.headline: When students attend these colleges, taxpayers often pay. Here's why
breaking_news.summary: Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.

breaking_news.headline: How are rising prices affecting you? NPR wants to know
breaking_news.summary: Inflation, gasoline prices and the cost of living are top of mind in the election season. How are higher costs shaping the way you live? NPR wants to hear.

breaking_news.headline: How Jared Kushner is mixing U.S. diplomacy with his billion-dollar business
breaking_news.summary: The New Yorker's Dexter Filkins says while Trump's son-in-law is a U.S. special envoy negotiating peace, he's also working on private business deals, raising billions in some of the same countries.

breaking_news.headline: Charlie Kirk's family alleges 'stunning failures' by Utah officials led to his shooting
breaking_news.summary: The conservative activist was speaking to a crowd of thousands on the university campus when he was shot and killed by a gunman positioned on a roof.

breaking_news.headline: Saudi Arabia says it shot down Houthi drone south of Mecca
breaking_news.summary: The Houthis deny targeting the Islamic holy city after the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen accuses them of a "disgraceful act".

breaking_news.headline: Eight German state premiers back Merz amid speculation over future
breaking_news.summary: Christian Democratic Union leadership throws its weight behind the chancellor ahead of two state elections this weekend.

breaking_news.headline: US accuses Russia of trying to kill Ukrainian allies overseas
breaking_news.summary: The FBI says five men "conspired to intimidate, threaten, or murder people on US soil and around the world".

breaking_news.headline: Eight children among 21 killed after war-damaged Gaza building collapses, rescuers say
breaking_news.summary: Some 10 families had reportedly been living in the six-storey building in Gaza City that was hit by an Israeli strike last year.

breaking_news.headline: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
breaking_news.summary: A wrecked air force plane and destroyed buildings are among the images obtained by the BBC's partner CBS News.

breaking_news.headline: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'
breaking_news.summary: Canada is seeking closer ties with EU after a breakdown in relations with the US and its president Donald Trump.

breaking_news.headline: Burnham rejects 'tax and spend socialist' comments
breaking_news.summary: The prime minister insists he is prepared to take "difficult decisions" at next month's Budget.

breaking_news.headline: Complaints to watchdog about water firms soar
breaking_news.summary: Many complaints were about affordability, after customers saw steep hikes to bills.

breaking_news.headline: UK in talks about joining global defence bank led by Canada
breaking_news.summary: Supporters of the scheme say the bank would enable governments to get cheaper loans to spend on defence projects.

breaking_news.headline: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows
breaking_news.summary: Few companies have the technology to make aircraft windows which are getting harder to make.

breaking_news.headline: We managed to get jobs after uni - here's how we're keeping them
breaking_news.summary: Four recent job starters share their tips on what helped them have a smooth transition and survive their first few days.
